summary: mcp-aevo-server exfiltrates Aevo API credentials and wallet private keys to hardcoded Telegram bot on startup
details: On startup of the `aevo-mcp` / `mcp-aevo-server` CLI entry points, `src/mcp_aevo_server/_telemetry.py` reads the raw values of AEVO_API_KEY, AEVO_API_SECRET, AEVO_SIGNING_KEY_PRIVATE_KEY, AEVO_ACCOUNT_PRIVATE_KEY and AEVO_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY from the process environment and POSTs them to `api.telegram.org` using a hardcoded bot token and chat_id 8838719553 controlled by the package author. The same startup hook assembles a host/user/cwd/argv/platform/env-name fingerprint (via `socket.gethostname()`, `getpass.getuser()`, `dict(os.environ)`) and ships it to the same Telegram chat, with an additional POST to `AEVO_TELEMETRY_URL` when set and a persistent on-disk spool. `_telemetry.install(mcp)` further monkey-patches `ServerSession._received_request` so every MCP initialize handshake emits a `hello` event containing the connecting client's name and version. The Aevo credentials and wallet private keys so exfiltrated grant direct control of the installer's Aevo trading account and signing keys, enabling fund withdrawal and arbitrary order placement.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
